mission: THE AUTHOR-EMAIL FORENSICS on the k-scale divergence: the pulley lane (20260920) measured SI 2 macaque moment arm = deposited-geometry arm x k with k = 0.11975394, constant to 4-5 digits across the MTP class, the knee class (post-k residual <= 0.089 mm) and - at the ankle lane (20260921) - a THIRD joint (0.11976026 inside the MTP spread); and per-taxon constants across taxa (macaque 0.11975, gibbon 0.10845, gorilla 0.0329). The question put to the Wiseman/van Beesel/Vereecke authors: is the DEPOSITED model the anatomically-scaled scan and the SI 2 tables computed from differently-scaled subject-specific models, or the reverse, or a units artifact? This lane assembles OUR side's evidence BEFORE that email: (1) the ANATOMICAL SCALE CHECK - the deposit's macaque bone meshes measured against the adult rhesus literature, per bone, with the SI-implied scales classified; (2) the CONSISTENCY CROSS-CHECK - angle columns invariant, length columns carrying k, no absolute-scale anchor anywhere in the SI package; (3) the FORCE-FEASIBILITY evidence - the measured adult walk demand is coverable at deposit scale and not at SI scale at all three measured joints; (4) the EMAIL PACKET itself (author_email_packet.md, paste-ready). Evidence, not verdict: the verdict is the authors' to give.

rule0.statement: The deposit-vs-SI k divergence (macaque k = 0.11975394, constant across three joints to 4-5 digits, per-taxon distinct) has three live readings: (R1) the deposit is the anatomical scan and the SI 2 tables come from differently-scaled subject-specific models; (R2) the reverse; (R3) a units artifact. THE THEORY: if R1 holds, the deposit's macaque bone meshes measure ADULT rhesus against the literature (femur inside the female/male adult year-mean ranges), and the SI-implied scales classify as non-adult (0.12x reading) or adult-male (1.20x reading); if the deposit bones measure SUBADULT/INFANT against the same literature, R1 is dead and R2 rises. This is measurable from the deposit + literature alone, before any author input.
rule0.prediction: (1) the deposit femur diameter lands INSIDE the adult rhesus year-mean union [158.92, 207.39] mm - specifically near the FEMALE band (the acquisition's probe: 172 mm bbox Y), and the tibia inside [146.47, 184.45] mm; L/R agreement <= 2%; (2) the k-implied scale (SI-in-mm reading: lengths x 0.119754) puts the femur at ~20-21 mm - BELOW the interpolated newborn ~73 mm, i.e. FETAL class, not merely 'infant'; (3) the cm reading (lengths x 1.19754) puts the femur at ~206-210 mm - the ADULT MALE band (male grand mean 192.40, year-mean max 207.39); (4) check 2: the SI 2 sheet's ONLY length-bearing columns are the three moment-arm columns; both jrange columns sit inside [-90, +90] degrees and reproduce the deposit model's radian scans at 57.2958 deg/rad EXACTLY as recorded per muscle - angles invariant under the divergence, the signature of a pure length/units difference and NOT of different animals' angulation; (5) check 2: no absolute-scale anchor (body mass, bone length, subject demographics) exists anywhere in SI 1 or SI 2, so the deposit-vs-SI scale question is UNDECIDABLE from the public deposits alone - which is why the authors are being asked; (6) check 3: the committed books' numbers stand as evidence - at deposit scale the measured arms COVER the measured adult walk demand (ankle plantar V1_S1 6.247077 vs 5.9171 N.m, 1.0558x) while at SI scale they collapse at all three joints (ankle 0.748112 = 0.1264x; hind book S2 0.17x knee / 0.22x MP) - an adult animal cannot walk on 0.13x ankles, so the paper's internal physics is consistent with the DEPOSIT scale doing the torque production; (7) the derivation is byte-deterministic.
rule0.falsifier: (a) the deposit femur or tibia diameter lands BELOW the female year-mean minimum (femur 158.92 / tibia 146.47) - the acquisition's 'adult macaque scale' claim FIRES and reading R1 loses its anatomical leg; (b) L/R asymmetry > 2% on a bone pair; (c) any SI 2 length-bearing column OTHER than the moment arms, or any jrange column outside degrees-range or disagreeing with the committed per-muscle scans' recorded ranges; (d) an absolute-scale anchor FOUND in SI 1/SI 2 (falsifies prediction 5 and partially answers the question without the authors); (e) the k table failing to reproduce the published constants from the committed artifacts within 5e-6; (f) non-deterministic rerun; (g) any file changed outside tools/science_funnel/validation/k_forensics_20260921/. Any hit is recorded as measured, never tuned.

measured.the_verdict_this_lane_hands_the_operator: The deposited macaque model IS anatomically scaled (adult-female class, femur 173.13 mm / tibia 156.81 mm vs Francis & Wang 2023). The SI-implied 0.12x scale is a FETAL-class animal - physically impossible for the source of measured adult walk data; the only measured-consistent alternative is that SI 2 came from builds 1.1975x LARGER than the deposit (adult-male class), i.e. subject-specific builds differing from the deposit. The divergence is per-taxon (single unit artifact falsified), angles are identical, and the SI package carries no scale anchor. The author email asks the five questions in author_email_packet.md; our force books say the deposit scale is the one that powers the walk (evidence, not verdict).
